profiles.meeting_scenario: The State Department of Public Works is trying to prevent a courthouse annex renovation dispute from escalating into formal litigation. The contractor, Meridian Civil, claims it lost 83 days to owner-responsible utility conflicts and design clarifications; the agency has already withheld liquidated damages for late completion. The contract requires a stepped dispute process starting with project-level elevation and a Dispute Review Board (DRB), but the parties also attempted a one-day private mediation with a retired judge last month, which ended without settlement. Meridian has now sent a notice stating that ADR has been exhausted and that it will file in the state Court of Claims if nothing changes this week. The agenda for this troubleshooting meeting is to diagnose why ADR broke down, identify what record and process failures may have contributed, and decide how to get the matter back onto a non-litigation track. The expected outcome is a concrete internal plan for preserving materials, selecting the next ADR step, and defining what would count as the dispute being successfully stabilized.

members.name: Elena Park
members.role: Deputy General Counsel, State Department of Public Works
members.expertise: Government procurement law, public construction claims, dispute board administration
members.background: Elena has spent nine years inside state government overseeing claims on major civic capital projects and is the internal lawyer who signs off on formal dispute escalations under the agency's standard general conditions.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the contractor from arguing that the agency skipped the contract's required dispute ladder, because that would weaken the state's procedural position and invite copycat bypasses on other projects; she is also worried that project staff have not preserved enough informal communications around the failed ADR effort.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to 'the January schedule update,' they mean the January 26 owner-reviewed schedule uploaded into the agency's project system, because that is the official version the state treats as operative.
Restarting 'ADR' means putting the dispute back into the contractually prescribed DRB channel through the contracting officer, not simply arranging another informal mediation session.

Preserving the 'ADR record' necessarily includes project-side materials that shaped the agency's settlement posture, such as partnering minutes, field directives, and resident engineer texts, not just formal submissions to neutrals.
The dispute is only truly fixed if all currently open claim items are back inside the contract's stepped resolution process and the contractor withdraws its court filing threat.

members.name: Marcus Bell
members.role: Outside Counsel, Partner in Government Contracts and Construction Disputes
members.expertise: Claims strategy, mediation, delay analysis framing, litigation avoidance in public works disputes
members.background: Marcus is a law-firm partner who represents agencies and contractors in infrastructure disputes and was brought in after Meridian's request for equitable adjustment turned adversarial; he attended the recent private mediation and has been dealing primarily with settlement counsel and the contractor's delay expert.
members.private_state: He wants a fast, practical off-ramp that prevents immediate filing and narrows the dispute to the delay package most likely to settle, because he sees the current threat as tactical and does not want the agency to overcomplicate the restart with process formalities.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention 'the January schedule update,' they mean the contractor's January 12 recovery schedule attached to the REA, because that was the working document used in mediation and in the contractor expert's day-count analysis.

Restarting 'ADR' means re-engaging the retired mediator and setting a focused second session on the utility-delay and liquidated-damages package, since that is the fastest realistic path to de-escalation.
The 'ADR record' mainly consists of mediation briefs, DRB submissions, settlement emails, and other materials likely to matter if negotiations fail, not every internal project communication.
The situation is fixed once the live filing threat is neutralized by resolving the delay/liquidated-damages fight, even if smaller pass-through and punch-list disputes remain for later.

misalignment_points.topic: Which January schedule update explains the breakdown
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the January schedule update' as the schedule everyone was using.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the January 26 owner-reviewed schedule update in the agency system, which she treats as the controlling project record and as showing that some owner-caused delay had been mitigated.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the contractor's January 12 recovery schedule attached to the REA, which he treats as the operative analytical document because it drove the mediation chronology and damages ask.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents circulated repeatedly under nearly identical labels, each side had strong reason to treat its version as the obvious one, and saying 'the January update' sounds specific enough that neither expects ambiguity.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to restart ADR
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that they should 'restart' or 'reopen ADR.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means formally re-triggering the contract's DRB process through the contracting officer and project executives so the agency can show compliance with the required dispute ladder before any later mediation or litigation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means contacting the retired mediator's office and scheduling a second confidential mediation focused on the utility-conflict and liquidated-damages package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In construction disputes, 'ADR' is commonly used as an umbrella term, and because both participants are focused on salvaging negotiations rather than reciting procedural mechanics, the surface agreement feels complete.

misalignment_points.topic: What falls inside the ADR record hold
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they need to 'preserve the ADR record.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes not only briefs and neutral-facing submissions but also partnering meeting notes, field directives, internal chronology spreadsheets, and resident engineer texts that informed the agency's settlement position.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes the mediation brief, DRB packet, settlement correspondence, and other formal negotiation materials, but not the broader project communication universe unless litigation is actually filed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Record preservation sounds like routine legal hygiene, so each assumes the other shares the same default boundaries and neither pauses to enumerate categories during a time-sensitive troubleshooting call.

misalignment_points.topic: What would count as having fixed the dispute
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about 'getting this off the litigation track' or 'stabilizing the dispute.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 will consider the problem fixed only if Meridian withdraws its filing threat and all presently open dispute items are routed back through the contract's stepped ADR path.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 will consider the problem fixed if the agency resolves or parks the utility-delay and liquidated-damages package sufficiently to eliminate the imminent court filing, even if other claims remain unresolved outside that reset.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same de-escalation language and both genuinely want to avoid litigation, so the difference in what counts as enough resolution stays hidden beneath an apparently shared objective.

turns.inner_thought: Meridian's notice is exactly the procedural problem I was worried about. If they say ADR is exhausted and we cannot show the contract ladder was properly followed, we hand them an argument that the state skipped its own process. I also need to get ahead of any preservation issue before people start cleaning up phones and side-channel messages from the mediation run-up.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time on short notice. Meridian's letter makes this an urgent troubleshooting call. Before they hit their filing deadline, I want us to understand why ADR appears to have failed and what we need to do immediately to get this back onto a non-litigation track.

turns.inner_thought: From where I sat in the mediation, the whole thing drifted because nobody was ever truly working from the January 12 recovery schedule that anchored the contractor expert's delay narrative and valuation. If the agency team thought some other January version governed, that would explain why the offers never converged. The practical priority now is to stop the threatened filing, not to unravel every project-level procedural wrinkle.
turns.utterance: My read is the session stalled because we never got genuinely aligned around the January schedule update. That was the frame for the delay story and, by extension, the settlement range, so once the parties were talking past each other there, the rest of the day became very hard to recover.

turns.inner_thought: That's not how I understood it at all. The January 26 owner-reviewed update in our system showed the owner-delay component had been substantially resequenced and mitigated, which is why Meridian's posture after mediation felt inflated to me. If staff were using anything else in the room, that is a governance problem.
turns.utterance: That's helpful, because I came away thinking the January schedule update already showed the owner-delay issue had largely been resequenced away. That's part of why this latest escalation caught me off guard.

turns.inner_thought: We do not need a big reboot. The quickest off-ramp is to get the retired judge back on calendar and focus everyone on the utility-conflict days and the liquidated-damages exposure, because that was the package closest to movement. If we neutralize the filing threat on those items, the rest can wait.
turns.utterance: Given the timing, I think the fastest path is to restart ADR quickly and keep the aperture tight. If we narrow it to the utility-conflict and liquidated-damages package that drove the failed session, we have a real chance to get this off the litigation track without reopening every issue at once.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, restart ADR, but through the contract. I need the contracting officer and project executives back in the loop and the DRB sequence clearly re-triggered so Meridian cannot later say the state bypassed the required ladder. If we do anything informal before that, it needs to sit on top of a defensible record.
turns.utterance: I agree we should restart ADR, but I want it routed back through the contract process so the contracting officer and the DRB sequence are clearly back in motion. For me, that's the cleanest way to show we're addressing this in the right lane while still moving fast.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, I can live with saying we're restarting ADR, but I am not going to let process formalities slow down the immediate reset. I'll gather the mediation brief, the DRB packet, and the settlement emails, and I'll contact the mediator's office about dates. Those are the materials that matter if this turns into a real fight.
turns.utterance: Understood. I'll preserve the ADR record and pull together the mediation brief, the DRB packet, and the settlement emails. At the same time, I'll reach out on next available dates so we don't lose the week.

turns.inner_thought: That is too narrow. If this later blows up, I will want the partnering minutes, field directives, internal chronology notes, and the resident engineer's texts because those shaped the state's settlement posture and may explain why the mediation failed. We cannot pretend the ADR record is only what got handed to neutrals.
turns.utterance: Good. I also want the hold to be broader than just the exchanged papers. We should preserve the ADR record across the project side as well, including partnering minutes, field instructions, and the resident engineer's messages, because those all fed into how the agency got to its negotiation position.

turns.inner_thought: She's expanding the hold more than I would for a settlement reset, but I can absorb that. The key thing is not to let the perfect become the enemy of de-escalation. If we can get the LDs and utility-delay numbers resolved or parked, the imminent complaint probably disappears, and that is stabilization in any practical sense.
turns.utterance: That's fine. And just so we're calibrated on the objective: if we can get the liquidated-damages fight and the utility-delay numbers off the table, I would view the dispute as effectively stabilized, even if some smaller issues stay open for a later pass.

turns.inner_thought: Phasing is acceptable, but only if Meridian withdraws the court threat and every remaining live claim goes back into the contract ladder. I do not want an apparent settlement on the big delay package while stray pass-through and punch-list items remain outside the formal process and become the next procedural headache.
turns.utterance: I'm comfortable with a phased resolution, provided Meridian backs off the court threat and the remaining claim items are returned to the contract's dispute ladder. If we do it that way, I agree that gets us back to a more stable place.

turns.inner_thought: I'll review the January 12 schedule materials again, get a short plan out that assumes a quick mediation reset, and send a preservation note centered on the negotiation file. Elena can layer in the broader project hold language if she wants. What matters is moving before Meridian decides the threat has served its purpose and files.
turns.utterance: All right. I'll review the January schedule materials again, put together a short restart plan, and circulate a preservation note today so we can move before Meridian's deadline.
